composition.serve_who: This sheet (21 of 27, section AFT, SWS_108-1_AFT PLC.dwg) details three WAGO 750-508 2-channel digital output modules in the AFT PLC rack (positions 13, 14, 15 under CPU 750-8213). Each module's two channels drive a pair of solenoid coils identified as EV-10.x A/B pairs, each pair named for a specific piece of equipment: EV-10.1A/B = transom door, EV-10.2A/B = deck door, EV-10.3A/B = mainsheet traveler. Per the mapping table, transom door -> 260-transom-door, deck door -> 260-deck-door, mainsheet traveller -> 840-cariboni-hydraulic-cylinders. The EV-10.x identifiers are hydraulic-manifold pilot functions (PVEO/PVEU type established on hydraulic sheets, e.g. AFT sailing/AFT mast sailing manifolds) — this sheet only shows the PLC-side wiring driving them via a Connector Type I field connector (detailed on sheet 4). The rack layout itself (module positions, CPU, coupler) is infrastructure belonging to the AFT PLC rack node.

equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: DO-03 module (POS.13) channels are explicitly labeled 'transom door CLOSE (EV 10.1A)' and 'transom door OPEN (EV 10.1B)', a direct name match to the transom door node. EV-10.1 pilot type (PVED ON/OFF) is established on the AFT_blockC hydraulic sheet and is retained here, not downgraded to a bare solenoid.

functions.label: Door close command
functions.sheet_region: left column, module POS.13, CH01 (upper output pair)
functions.what_it_does: Digital output channel 1 of the DO-03 module energises the transom door CLOSE pilot solenoid (EV 10.1A), driving the hydraulic actuator to close the transom door.
key_components: PVED ON/OFF pilot solenoid EV-10.1A (established type, hydraulic sheet)
module common/reference terminal A1/A2 (module supply) — voltage on CH01 output measured relative to the module's own common (A2) terminal, per WAGO 750-508 module wiring

flow_scenarios.path: PLC DO-03 CH01 output off → EV-10.1A pilot un-energised → transom door hydraulic circuit holds last position (no close command)

PLC DO-03 CH01 output on (24V relative to module common) → wired down through DO-03 terminal block → Connector Type I pin (see sheet 4) → field cable → EV-10.1A pilot solenoid coil → hydraulic manifold shifts spool → transom door cylinder drives CLOSE

infrastructure.system_name: AFT PLC I/O Rack (WAGO) — DO module positions 13-15
facts: Position 13: WAGO 750-508 2-channel digital output module, tag DO-03
Position 14: WAGO 750-508 2-channel digital output module, tag DO-04
Position 15: WAGO 750-508 2-channel digital output module, tag DO-05
Each module has A1/A2 bus/power terminals feeding the rack backplane; A1/A2 are module supply/bus terminals, not field I/O
Field wiring from each module's channel pair routes to earth/ground terminal then to a dedicated 4-pin circular 'Connector Type I' plug (pinout/mating detail on sheet 4)
No local switches, panel switches, alarm taps, or separate protective fuses/breakers shown for these output circuits on this sheet — control originates purely from PLC DO channels

Rev history: Rev 0 (21/03/2023 first issue); Rev 4 (05/05/2026) 'SUBSTITUTE WINCHES MODULES FROM DIGITAL TO ANALOG' — note this revision note pertains to winch modules elsewhere in the set, not to these three door/traveler modules shown here

uncertainties: Exact pilot valve device type (PVEO vs PVED vs PVEU) for EV-10.1, EV-10.2, EV-10.3 could not be independently confirmed from this sheet alone; type is inherited from cross-sheet convention only where an equivalent EV was matched on the hydraulic sheets. For EV-10.2 (deck door) and EV-10.3 (mainsheet traveler) no direct hydraulic-sheet pilot-type record was found in the established facts provided, so 'PLED/PVEU' cannot be asserted with certainty for those two — recorded generically as 'per hydraulic/sailing manifold sheet' pending confirmation.

Whether the module 'common' reference is a per-module M terminal (WAGO-style) or the vessel's 24V negative rail could not be confirmed from this sheet's terminal labeling (only A1/A2 supply terminals and +/- channel pairs are shown, no explicit 'M' common terminal marked) — flagged rather than assumed.
